To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have established a classification system applicable to plant LTR-retrospons based on phylogenetic analyses of their polyprotein sequences, and have created a database of LTR-retroposon protein domains that reflects this classification and provides a reference system for annotation of these elements.

we have created a database of retroelement encoded polyprotein domains from a large number of plant species that reflects their phylogenetic relatedness, and we have used the database to establish a comprehensive classification system of plant LTR retrotransposons.
we have created a database of plant LTR retrotransposons that reflects their phylogenetic diversity and provides a reference classification for these elements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of bioinformatics tools for the study of plant LTR-transposable elements.
the development of bioinformatics tools and methods for the identification and characterization of plant repetitive sequences, including LTR-retroelements.
the evolution of LTR-retrosposons, which is a very important topic in evolutionary genomics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have created a new classification system for LTR-retrotranposon polyprotein domains and a database of retrotrnansposon encoded protein domains.
the phylogenetic relationships between LTR-retroelement polyprotein domains are highly congruent with the phylogeny of the plants themselves.

the REXdb database and the classification system it implements is a powerful tool that will facilitate the annotation of plant LTR-RTs and will be of a great help for the analysis of their impact on plant genomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided a reference classification of LTR retrotransposons in plants that is applicable for efficient annotation of these elements in plant genomes and that will facilitate comparative studies of LTR retroelements.
we developed a new classification system for plant LTR-retrosposons based on phylogenetic analysis of polyprotein domains.
REXdb is a reference database of retrotransposable element protein domains and their phylogenetic classification.
The main takeaway from our work is that

phylogenetic relationships among plant LTR-retrospons can be efficiently and reliably inferred from the analysis of their polyprotein domain sequences, which are readily extracted from the available genome sequences.
the phylogenetic relationships among retrotransposons are much better reflected by their polyprotein domain composition than by their overall nucleotide sequences.

the phylogenetic classification of LTR elements can be achieved by analyzing only three protein domains (RT, INT, and RH) and that the classification is consistent across the whole range of plant species.
